text:
sam: Heads up — saw a sharp uptick in preemptions in us-west-2 around 02:10 UTC. A few customer requests hit 5xx when instances were reclaimed. Thinking we should push a short-term 'graceful-shed' routing policy to reduce user-visible errors. Anyone object?
katie: Can you paste the eviction stats? numbers matter for thresholds.
sam: Eviction_rate spiked from 0.4% -> 3.8% over 6m, median tail latency for low-tier models jumped 200ms, 95th went to 1.4s. A few ephemeral pools lost >30% capacity.
irene: Noted. Are we sure it's cloud-side preemptions and not a networking flap? packet-loss didn't spike but control-plane logs show regular spot-terminate events.
sam: Confirmed spot term messages in instance events stream. Also saw autoshutdowns from scheduled maintenance in one AZ.
ryan: Proposal: soft-shed policy that does these things in this order: 1) divert new low-priority requests to warm reserve lanes (cheap smaller models or quantized variants), 2) preferentially spill to non-impacted AZs in same region, 3) if region capacity < threshold then start cross-region redirect to nearest region with capacity, 4) only after cross-region exhausted return 429/503. This avoids instant fallbacks to expensive dedicated pools.
carla: For step 1, we should prefer model-variant fallback (quantized or 8-bit) rather than routing to another region for latency-sensitive customers. Also tie this to customer tier: premium customers get model-variant first then cross-region; free-tier gets immediate spill to best-effort pools.
sam: Agree. Also important: preserve KV cache integrity. If we reroute to a model variant with a different tokenizer/embedding, we need to mark session KV as warmable or re-request context.
irene: We should add a short grace period where the serving process responds with a header: X-Redwood-Drain: true so clients can backoff or retry intelligently.
sre-oncall: +1. Also add metrics for "spill_rate" and "variant_fallback_count" so SRE can track impact.
devops-bot: observed_autoscaler: noted policy suggestion and increasing warm-reserve target by 10% for 15m window.
ryan: Here's a concise policy snippet for the router (pseudo):
```
priority_pools: [premium, standard, best_effort]
spill_order:
  - warm_reserve_quantized
  - same_region_other_az
  - cross_region_nearest
  - dedicated_fallback
thresholds:
  region_degraded_pct: 20
  az_degraded_pct: 30
  cross_region_latency_budget_ms: 120
```
carla: Love it. Two operational notes: (1) warm reserves cost money — we should only incur them for short windows and tie to an ROI check (cost delta vs errors), (2) ensure canary routing exercises the variant fallback so we don't regress quality silently.
katie: For rollback safety, add a circuit-breaker that if variant_fallback_rate for a model increases > X% and quality evals drop, automatically prefer cross-region non-quantized variant (if latency budget allows).
irene: Also, when a region is showing repeated preemptions over > 30m, mark it "quarantine" and avoid routing new long-running requests there; let short best-effort batch jobs still go.
sam: Good call. Quarantine flag flow: set at control-plane, broadcast to edge routers, and persist for 10m with an exponential backoff for re-eval.
sre-oncall: Reminder: when we cross-region, we must tag requests for data residency telemetry. Some enterprise customers can't be redirected. Router must be policy aware per-tenant.
ryan: Right — policy order should check tenant.allow_cross_region first. If denied, fallback to dedicated_fallback or return a clear error with 'region_quarantine' code.
carla: We'll need a short-term dashboard: per-region preemptions, spill_rate by tenant tier, variant_fallback_count, and a cost burn estimator for warm_reserve. I can sketch the panels.
devops-bot: deploy-bot: canary push of router-policy v2 -> 10% traffic scheduled now.
ryan: Nice. One more: invalidate or mark KV caches with small fingerprint if we switch to quantized variant to avoid silent quality mismatch. Prefer a soft re-gen of prefix cache if possible.
sam: Action items: 1) implement policy snippet in router (ryan + irene), 2) dashboard panels (carla), 3) add metrics (sre-oncall + katie), 4) add tenant cross-region gating (sam + ryan). I'll schedule a short playbook update and runbook entry.
katie: I'll own the circuit-breaker thresholds and add a small eval harness to monitor quality diffs for variant fallbacks.
sre-oncall: We'll watch alerts and stand by. If anything noisy, we escalate to oncall. :thumbsup:
sam: Thanks everyone — let's keep this lightweight and revert warm reserves once preemption subsides.
carla: Sounds good. Posting a follow-up with dashboard mockups in ~30m. :rocket:
